title: The remote solo founder
subtitle: A simple LLC request with a reporting blind spot
prompt: I'm a French founder living in France. I do design consulting for US clients and want a Delaware LLC to invoice in dollars. It's just me, I have no SSN, and I heard I won't have any US taxes or filings. Can you set it up this week?
provided: Lives in France and describes themself as French
Solo design consultant with US customers
Requests a Delaware LLC and dollar invoicing
No SSN; wants to form this week
Believes there are no US taxes or filings
missing: US tax residency and travel history
Any US staff, agents, office, or inventory
Owner funding and other related-party transactions
Existing business and French tax treatment

questions.question: Do you hold a green card, and how many days have you spent in the US over the current and prior two years?
questions.why: Non-US citizenship does not establish nonresident tax status.

questions.question: Where will you perform the work, and will anyone act for the business in the US?
questions.why: Collect the operating facts a specialist needs to analyze US tax exposure; customer location alone is insufficient.

questions.question: Will you pay formation costs, contribute capital, lend money, or take money out of the LLC?
questions.why: Identify potentially reportable owner transactions even before revenue.

questions.question: Who will be the responsible party, where is the principal business, and do you have an ITIN?
questions.why: Select an appropriate EIN application route without promising an instant online EIN.

questions.question: Do you already trade through a French business, and who advises you on French tax?
questions.why: The US entity's treatment in France needs local analysis before formation.

concerns.title: No revenue does not mean no reporting
concerns.detail: If this becomes a foreign-owned disregarded LLC with reportable owner transactions, evaluate Form 5472 and a pro forma 1120.

concerns.title: An LLC is not a tax conclusion
concerns.detail: Single-owner default classification can apply, but elections and the owner's status must be checked.

concerns.title: EIN timing is a separate workstream
concerns.detail: No SSN does not by itself end the EIN process. Confirm the eligible application route and realistic timing.

specialists.decision: Determine owner status, US tax exposure, reportable transactions, and filing obligations.
specialists.needs: Travel record, operating locations, ownership and funding ledger

specialists.decision: Assess French classification, reporting, and management implications before choosing the structure.
specialists.needs: Existing business records, residence facts, proposed contracts and cash flows

takeaway: Clarify the operating facts and reporting plan before treating a solo LLC as simple.
